DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Hypertension (Benign Hypertension).

The clinical picture of a 5-year-old boy with normal blood pressure readings, no family history, normal renal function, and no signs of renal disease on urinalysis and electrolytes makes a secondary cause like renovascular hypertension or renal parenchymal disease highly unlikely. The current data supports a diagnosis of benign or idiopathic hypertension, likely related to lifestyle factors or transient physiological causes.
